primary_goals: Reduce excess facial or body hair
Help my body respond better to insulin
Improve my chances of ovulating & getting pregnant

questions.label: Blood Pressure, Resting Heart Rate & SpO2
questions.description: Basic vitals -- high blood pressure or resting heart rate with low oxygen can point to HPA-axis (stress) overactivation.

questions.label: DHEA-S (Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulfate)
questions.reference: 83-377 µg/dL (age 18-30, Mayo Clinic Laboratories; isolated >350 = Adrenal)
questions.description: DHEA-S is an adrenal androgen; a level far above normal is a strong sign of the Adrenal phenotype. Reference range is age-dependent and narrows with age (Mayo Clinic Laboratories, test DHES1); levels above roughly 600 µg/dL specifically warrant prompt medical evaluation for a possible androgen-secreting adrenal tumor.

questions.label: Fasting Cortisol (AM) / Salivary Cortisol Curve
questions.description: Cortisol is your main stress hormone; an abnormal morning level suggests HPA-axis dysregulation.

questions.label: Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10)
questions.reference: Cohen, Kamarck & Mermelstein, 1983 -- 0-13 low stress, 14-26 moderate, 27-40 high stress

fields.label: In the last month, how often were you upset by something that happened unexpectedly?
In the last month, how often did you feel unable to control the important things in your life?
In the last month, how often did you feel nervous or stressed?
In the last month, how often did you feel confident about your ability to handle your personal problems?
In the last month, how often did you feel that things were going your way?
In the last month, how often did you find you could not cope with everything you had to do?
In the last month, how often were you able to control irritations in your life?
In the last month, how often did you feel on top of things?
In the last month, how often were you angered by things outside of your control?
In the last month, how often did difficulties pile up so high you could not overcome them?

questions.description: The Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) is a widely used, validated 10-question tool measuring how stressful your life has felt over the past month. Answer each based on how often you felt that way -- there are no right or wrong answers.

questions.label: PHQ-2 (Depression Screener)
questions.reference: Kroenke, Spitzer & Williams, 2003 -- score >= 3 suggests further evaluation

fields.label: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you had little interest or pleasure in doing things?
Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?

questions.description: The PHQ-2 is a standard 2-question clinical screening tool for low mood. It's a screen, not a diagnosis -- a higher score just means it's worth talking to a doctor or counselor about how you've been feeling lately.

questions.label: Sleep Duration & Quality (onset, awakenings, wake time)
questions.description: Short or broken sleep raises cortisol and worsens adrenal-driven symptoms.

questions.label: Fatigue (feeling worn out easily)

fields.label: Do you feel worn out easily?

questions.description: Feeling worn out even after rest can be a sign of ongoing stress-axis overload.

questions.label: Worried (about past, future, health)
questions.description: Frequent worry about the past, future, or health is a common stress-axis symptom.

questions.label: Poor concentration
questions.description: Trouble focusing for long periods can be linked to chronic stress.

questions.label: Shallow breathing
questions.description: Fast, shallow chest-breathing (over 20 breaths/min) is a physical sign of a stressed nervous system.

questions.label: Frequent mood swings
questions.reference: Sudden irritability, anger, or mood drops
questions.description: Sudden irritability, anger, or low mood can reflect stress-hormone swings.

questions.label: Menstrual Cycle Length & Regularity
questions.reference: Regular 21-35 day ovulatory cycles (abnormal > 45 days) -- 2018 International PCOS Guideline / Rotterdam oligoanovulation definition

fields.label: Are periods absent (amenorrhea) for over 45 days?

questions.description: Cycles shorter than 21 or longer than 35 days point toward ovarian/hormonal imbalance.

questions.label: Hirsutism Severity (excess facial/body hair on chest, chin, abdomen)
questions.description: Excess coarse hair on the face, chest, chin, or abdomen is a classic sign of high androgens.

questions.label: Pattern Hair Loss / Androgenic Alopecia (scalp thinning)
questions.description: Thinning hair on the scalp in a male-pattern distribution can be androgen-driven.

questions.label: Acne Characteristics (cystic, jawline, adult-onset)
questions.reference: Clear skin / absence of inflammatory acne
questions.description: Deep, cystic, or jawline acne that starts in adulthood is often androgen-linked.

questions.label: Pelvic Ultrasound Findings (polycystic ovary morphology)
questions.reference: < 20 follicles per ovary, volume < 10 ml (2018 International PCOS Guideline, ESHRE)
questions.description: An ultrasound showing many small follicles or an enlarged ovary supports the Rotterdam ultrasound criterion.

questions.label: Total Testosterone
questions.reference: 8-60 ng/dL (adult women; Endocrine Society / Mayo Clinic Laboratories)
questions.description: Total testosterone measures overall androgen levels in the blood.

questions.label: Free Testosterone
questions.reference: 0.13-1.08 ng/dL (age 20-30; Mayo Clinic Laboratories, test TTFB)
questions.description: Free testosterone is the biologically active portion not bound to protein.

questions.label: LH to FSH Ratio
questions.description: An LH:FSH ratio above roughly 2:1 is a classic ovarian/hormonal PCOS marker.

questions.label: Sex Hormone-Binding Globulin (SHBG)
questions.reference: 18-135 nmol/L (premenopausal women, ages 18-46; Mayo Clinic Laboratories, test SHBG1)
questions.description: Low SHBG lets more testosterone circulate freely, worsening androgen symptoms.

questions.label: History of Post-Pill Amenorrhea or Synthetic Hormone Use

fields.label: History of post-pill amenorrhea / synthetic hormone use?

questions.description: Periods that don't return for months after stopping birth control can unmask an underlying hormonal imbalance.

questions.label: Acne Characteristics (cystic, jawline, adult-onset)
questions.reference: Clear skin / absence of inflammatory acne
questions.description: The same acne pattern can also flag an inflammatory/immune driver, not just androgens.

questions.label: Joint Pain, Unexplained Swelling, or Food Sensitivities

fields.label: Joint pain, unexplained swelling, or food sensitivities?

questions.description: Unexplained joint pain, swelling, or food sensitivities can point to systemic inflammation.

questions.label: High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein (hs-CRP)
questions.reference: < 1.0 mg/L (AHA/CDC low cardiovascular-risk tier; Pearson et al., Circulation 2003)
questions.description: hs-CRP is a blood marker of low-grade, body-wide inflammation. <1.0 mg/L is the established lower-risk tier; 1.0-3.0 mg/L is average risk and >3.0 mg/L is higher risk (AHA/CDC scientific statement).

questions.label: Thyroid Panel (TSH, Free T3, Free T4, TPO Antibodies)
questions.reference: TSH 0.4-4.0 mIU/L (American Thyroid Association); TPO Ab negative
questions.description: Thyroid imbalances and thyroid antibodies often travel alongside inflammatory PCOS.

questions.label: Vitamin D3 (25-OH) & Serum Zinc
questions.reference: Vitamin D3 optimal target > 40 ng/mL / Serum Zinc 60-106 µg/dL (Mayo Clinic Laboratories)
questions.description: Low vitamin D or zinc can both contribute to and result from chronic inflammation. This app targets >40 ng/mL as an optimal vitamin D level; the 2011 Endocrine Society guideline's minimum "sufficient" cutoff is 30 ng/mL, and the 2024 update declined to endorse a single universal target.

questions.label: Daily EDC Exposure (plastics, pesticides, non-stick, cosmetics)
questions.description: Everyday exposure to plastics, pesticides, and other endocrine-disrupting chemicals can drive inflammation.

questions.label: Heavy Metal or Occupational Chemical Exposures
questions.description: Ongoing exposure to heavy metals or industrial chemicals is a less common but real inflammatory trigger.

questions.label: Gut Health Status (bloating, IBS, constipation, dysbiosis)
questions.reference: Normal daily bowel movements, no bloating

fields.label: If yes - is it severe / frequent (severe IBS or gut dysbiosis)?

questions.description: Bloating, IBS-type symptoms, or irregular bowel movements can signal gut-driven inflammation.

questions.label: Chronic Low-Grade Infections or Autoimmune History

fields.label: Chronic low-grade infections or autoimmune history?

questions.description: A personal history of autoimmune disease or frequent low-grade infections raises inflammatory risk.

questions.label: Sunlight Exposure (10am-4pm, >20 min/day) & deficiency symptoms
questions.reference: No bone/joint pain, muscle weakness, or slow wound healing

fields.label: Bone/joint pain, muscle weakness, or slow wound healing?

questions.description: Too little sun exposure can lower vitamin D and contribute to inflammation.

questions.label: Fasting Lipid Profile (Triglycerides & HDL)
questions.reference: Triglycerides < 150 mg/dL, HDL > 50 mg/dL, TG:HDL ratio < 2.0
questions.description: High triglycerides, low HDL, or a high triglyceride-to-HDL ratio are all signs of the same underlying metabolic dysfunction -- any one of them counts as a positive finding here.

questions.label: Height, Weight, BMI, and Waist-to-Hip Ratio (WHR)
questions.description: BMI and waist-to-hip ratio together flag insulin-resistance-related weight patterns.

questions.label: Presence of Acanthosis Nigricans (darkened skin patches)
questions.description: Dark, velvety skin patches (neck, underarms) are a visible sign of insulin resistance.

questions.label: History of Skin Tags
questions.description: Multiple skin tags are commonly associated with high insulin levels.

questions.label: Recurrent Fatigue, Brain Fog, or Energy Slumps After Meals

fields.label: Fatigue / brain fog / energy slumps after meals?

questions.description: Feeling foggy or sleepy after meals can indicate blood-sugar swings from insulin resistance.

questions.label: Fasting Glucose & Fasting Insulin
questions.description: Fasting glucose and insulin together are the core blood tests for insulin resistance. This app uses stricter early-warning thresholds than standard diabetes screening: the ADA standard fasting-glucose cutoffs are prediabetes 100-125 mg/dL and diabetes ≥126 mg/dL, and the standard fasting-insulin lab range is 2-25 µIU/mL (2-6 µIU/mL considered optimal) -- catching insulin resistance before it reaches those diagnostic thresholds is the point of PCOS-specific screening.

questions.label: HbA1c (Glycated Hemoglobin)
questions.description: HbA1c reflects your average blood sugar over the past ~3 months. This app flags earlier than standard diabetes screening (ADA prediabetes cutoff is 5.7%, diabetes ≥6.5%) to catch insulin resistance while it's still early.

questions.label: HOMA-IR Index
questions.description: HOMA-IR is a calculated score of how well your body responds to insulin. This app's ≥1.5 tick / >2.0 override thresholds are consistent with PCOS-specific insulin-resistance research; commonly cited general-population HOMA-IR cutoffs for insulin resistance range from 2.0-2.5.

questions.label: Daily Physical Activity Level

fields.label: Mostly sedentary / below regular moderate-to-vigorous activity?

questions.description: Low daily activity contributes to and worsens insulin resistance over time.

questions.label: Ultra-Processed Food & Refined Sugar Intake

fields.label: 2 or more ultra-processed / high-sugar meals per week?

questions.description: Frequent ultra-processed or high-sugar food spikes insulin and blood glucose.

questions.label: Sleep Apnea

fields.label: Do you have sleep apnea (stop breathing during sleep)?

questions.description: Sleep apnea is a strong driver of insulin resistance, independent of weight.

questions.label: Hypoxia (Shortness of Breath / Low Oxygen)

fields.label: Do you experience hypoxia (shortness of breath/low oxygen)?

questions.description: Low blood oxygen can worsen insulin resistance and metabolic strain.

questions.label: Body Type
questions.description: Obese and lean PCOS have different dietary requirements.
questions.reference: Self-reported body type; used only to tailor the diet/exercise plan, not scored against a 'normal' value

mitochondrial_axis.label: General Mitochondrial Dysfunction & Hypoxia Triggers
mitochondrial_axis.source: Section 2, Table 5 (screening axis, scored out of 4, not one of the 4 main phenotypes)

questions.label: Fatigue / Low Energy

fields.label: Are you feeling fatigued or low on energy most days?

questions.description: A simple everyday fatigue check, asked directly instead of screening for depression.

questions.label: Hypoxia Indicators (shallow breathing, low oxygen, anemia)
questions.reference: Cellular hypoxia impairs ovarian follicle maturation

fields.label: Shallow/chest breathing, low-oxygen symptoms, or anemia?

questions.description: Shallow breathing and anemia both reduce how much oxygen reaches your tissues.

questions.label: Sleep Apnea
questions.reference: Nocturnal hypoxia disrupts mitochondrial recovery during sleep

fields.label: Do you have sleep apnea (stop breathing during sleep)?

questions.description: Sleep apnea is asked on its own, separately from general hypoxia symptoms.

questions.label: Post-Exertional Malaise (feeling crashed after exercise)

fields.label: Feeling crashed / wiped out after exercise?

questions.description: Crashing or feeling wiped out after normal exercise can signal impaired cellular energy production.

questions.label: Sudden Detraining / Cessation of Competitive Sports

fields.label: Sudden stop of a previously active/competitive sport routine?

questions.description: Suddenly stopping regular sport/exercise can itself disrupt hormonal and energy balance.

overrides.label: Fasting Insulin > 10 µIU/mL or HOMA-IR > 2.0
overrides.source: Section 3, Key Biomarker Priority Overrules, bullet 1

overrides.label: Isolated DHEA-S > 350 µg/dL with normal insulin
overrides.reference: Confirms Adrenal Phenotype (isolated marked elevation, normal insulin). DHEA-S >600 µg/dL specifically is suggestive of an androgen-secreting adrenal tumor (Mayo Clinic Laboratories) and warrants urgent medical evaluation regardless of phenotype.
overrides.source: Section 3, Key Biomarker Priority Overrules, bullet 2

overrides.label: LH:FSH > 2:1 or post-pill amenorrhea
overrides.source: Section 3, Key Biomarker Priority Overrules, bullet 3

overrides.label: hs-CRP > 1.5 mg/L or severe IBS/gut dysbiosis
overrides.source: Section 3, Key Biomarker Priority Overrules, bullet 4

classification_rules.primary: Section 3: phenotype with the highest percentage of positive ticks (out of 10) is the primary/dominant driver.
classification_rules.mixed: Section 3: if two phenotypes tie for the highest tick count, classify as Mixed/Combination Phenotype requiring a dual-targeted protocol.
classification_rules.override_precedence: Section 3: a triggered biomarker override confirms its phenotype and can flip the tally-based classification. If overrides for two different phenotypes trigger simultaneously, classify as Mixed/Combination.
classification_rules.biomarker_support_note: Section 3: '3+ positive findings in key biomarkers' for a phenotype is surfaced as supporting evidence alongside the tally-based result.
